title: Archaeology Adventure
description:
Join Moley, our friendly archaeologist-in-training, as your guide on a hands-on journey through time.
From fieldwalking to excavation, discover the real techniques archaeologists use to reveal hidden histories and try your hand at becoming a history detective. Young explorers and curious minds of all ages can dig, discover, and decode clues from the past, learning how everyday objects help archaeologists piece together ancient lives.
Interactive activities and playful challenges invite visitors to get involved, whether you’re uncovering buried finds, recording discoveries, or interpreting intriguing artefacts.
A selection of objects from archaeological excavations across Kent will be on display, offering glimpses into the region’s rich and varied past, from Roman Britain to more recent history. These finds help tell the stories of the people who lived here and the landscapes they shaped.
With special loans from the Kent Archaeological Society, Cranbrook Museum, and the Guildhall Museum, Rochester, Archaeology Adventure celebrates the heritage of Kent through curiosity, creativity, and discovery. Come and dig a little deeper – who knows what you might find?

title: Activist Avenue
description:
Learn about the history of Tunbridge Wells in a way you’ve never seen before…
From the minds of the Young Producers comes a new trail full of untold stories – be the first to uncover the forgotten histories of radicals like Olive Walton, Jasper Sprange and Amelia Scott herself.
Across the Amelia, you will travel through the past and investigate the life of each pioneer from Tunbridge Wells’ history. Interact with their stories further by reading about their experiences and completing fun activities! Collect all the stamps along the way in your “Passport Through Time” and perhaps they will leave you a special reward…
An experience for all ages.
This project is part of our Unlocking Collections Programme, supported using public funding from the National Lottery through Arts Council England.

title: Home Education at The Amelia - Primary
description:
Join us at The Amelia for our monthly learning sessions open to home educated children across the borough.
Our learning sessions are linked to The Amelia’s collections, are based on enquiry-led learning and are rooted in the National Curriculum. Sessions provide unique opportunities for object-handling and inspiring activities to guide children and their families as they explore our galleries.
Duration: Standard sessions last 60 mins
We aim to provide a fully inclusive service for all our young visitors. Please let us know if there are any SPLD/ or accessibility needs we should be aware of so that we can help support all participants to engage with the session.
Please note, children must be accompanied by their parent/carers and remain their responsibility at all times.
Monthly themes:
8 September – Archaeology Adventure
Join us for a special exhibition-linked session. The group will start with an introduction to archaeology in the Learning Room, with the chance to explore artefacts and objects hands-on. The session will conclude in Archaeology Adventure, our current temporary exhibition.
13 October – The Story of the Wells – Local History
In this session, the group will discover how and why our town came into existence. Using artefacts to piece together its story from forest, to popular health resort, to holiday destination for a princess, the group will also find out why children from the East End of London would spend their summer holidays here 100 years ago!
10 November – Dinosaurs and Fossils
In this session, the group are cast as palaeontologists and explore clues about what the world was like millions of years ago. They have the chance to handle a range of fossils from The Amelia’s Collection to investigate how they were made and what they tell us about the past.
8 December – Generations of Joy
This session will take place off-site and provide an enriching opportunity for intergenerational engagement, with children and care-home residents taking part in Christmas-themed activities together.

Contact us to find out more before booking

title: Escapulario Workshop with Aitor Saraiba
description:
We have the pleasure of bringing acclaimed textile artist to The Amelia this autumn – Aitor Saraiba. If you love embroidery then this event is perfect for you.
A very special embroidery workshop, where you will learn to stitch while creating a beautiful and now iconic textile little amulet (Escapulario) by Aitor Saraiba. The artist, a defender of intuitive, creative, and pattern-free embroidery, will guide you through this transformative experience.
You will leave the workshop with your own handmade little amulet (Escapulario), created using the exclusive materials included in Aitor Saraiba’s custom kit.
Search Press have kindly given our attending audience a 20% discount code and will deliver your order to the Amelia when you buy Aitor’s new book. Use code AITORTA when you purchase using the link below. Please order before 9th October to ensure that your book will be available to collect at the event.
About the artist:Aitor Saraiba lives and works in a stone cabin in the valleys of Cantabria, northern Spain.
He has been working in drawing, textile art and ceramics for two decades, and his work has been exhibited all over the world, from Los Angeles to Tokyo, including Portugal, Italy, the United Kingdom, Africa and several cities in Spain.
Aitor Saraiba’s textile work explores different traditional techniques and brings them into his own unique world. He has revived traditional wool-working processes with his flock of sheep, in the mountains where he lives, uses natural dyes with silver, and employs all manner of darning and mending techniques to create stunning, unique artworks.
In 2022, the newspaper El País awarded him the ICON Artisan of the Year prize for his work in textiles and ceramics. He has also collaborated with numerous museum across Europe and beyond.
In Embroider, Mend and Sew, Aitor explores his textile process, wherein personal history and creativity intertwine.
Follow Aitor on Instagram at @aitorsaraiba, where he has over 156.5k followers, and at www.aitorsaraiba.com

title: An Evening with Jonny Hincks
description:
Join us for an entertaining evening with Jonny Hincks. Best known online to his fans as ‘GardenWithJonny’, Jonny is a Warwickshire-based gardening content creator, sharing his love for all things nature to his loyal following.
Johnny will be in conversation at our evening event, answering a range of questions about his garden of course, giving tips for your own garden, plus how it has supported his own journey with mental health.
There’s certain to be some laughter and fun along the way!
Jonny turns to his garden for joy and peace and is a big advocate for its positive impact on mental health and well being. He’s passionate about making gardening fun and accessible for everyone, which is why he has written Garden Yourself Happy!
Garden Yourself Happy
A Quirky, Practical Guide to Keeping You and Your Garden Thriving
Stay green, stay gorgeous, and find the joy in your garden with this big-hearted, relatable guide!
Gardening enthusiast Jonny Hincks – known by over 2 million followers online as @gardenwithjonny – has helped countless people to get out in their garden with his wholesome advice and whimsical humour. From dancing while he pots to singing on his shed’s roof, there’s never a dull day in Jonny’s garden.
As a firefighter by day, Jonny turns to his garden for joy and peace and is a big advocate for its positive impact on your mental health and well being. He’s passionate about making gardening fun and accessible for everyone, which is why he has written Garden Yourself Happy!
Discover the joy of getting outdoors with his quick, actionable jobs that fit into everyday life. You’ll learn how to keep your garden looking sharp in short, manageable bursts; as well as learn how to tackle longer-term jobs such as lawn care, composting, creating your garden vision and more.
Whether you’ve got a big garden, a tiny yard, a few pots on a balcony or just the itch to get growing, this is for you. With seasonal to-do lists and Jonny’s personal journey to becoming a garden geek, this is a big-hearted and practical guide to finding the joy in your garden.
About the author!
JONNY HINCKS, best known online to his fans as ‘GardenWithJonny’ is a Warwickshire-based gardening content creator, sharing his love for all things nature to his loyal following. Jonny’s online content ranges from his best gardening tips, to showcasing his warm and silly sense of humour through fun reels outdoors. When Jonny isn’t knee deep in soil, he works for the fire service, as a firefighter.

title: Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden
description:
A major print retrospective of one of Britain’s most celebrated artists
Experience Howard Hodgkin's vivid world of colour in this exhibition of prints spanning five decades.
Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden brings together more than thirty richly coloured prints by one of Britain's most distinctive modern artists. 
Spanning five decades, from 1966 to 2016, the exhibition offers an engaging introduction to Hodgkin's printmaking. It shows how he used colour, shape and texture to turn memories, places and personal encounters into vivid visual experiences. 
Hodgkin is best known as a painter, but he was also one of Britain's most important printmakers. Born in London in 1932, he developed a language of bold marks, layered surfaces and intense colour. Many of the prints in this exhibition are hand-coloured, giving them a physical presence and emotional depth that reward close looking. 
The works range from lyrical city scenes to images inspired by Hodgkin's long connection with India, as well as prints created for the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Although they can appear spontaneous, they were often made through a slow and highly considered process. Hodgkin experimented with techniques including etching and aquatint, combining them with hand-painting to create images of remarkable richness. 
Hodgkin's significance was recognised internationally during his lifetime. He won the Turner Prize in 1985, represented Britain at the Venice Biennale, and his work has been shown in major museums including Tate Britain, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and the Reina Sofía in Madrid. Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden invites visitors to experience an artist whose colour, feeling and imagination continue to resonate today.

A member of the Backman Trio, she performed across the UK and Finland, recording for YLE 1 and releasing their debut CD Fantasia in 2014.

She also teaches at the City of London School, the Centre for Young Musicians, TWGGS and The Judd School.
Marcus Andrews performs widely as a soloist, chamber musician and concerto pianist. He has performed all the Beethoven concerti with St Paul’s Sinfonia, and his debut CD features works by Beethoven and Medtner.
He studied at Trinity Laban, winning the Keyboard Silver Medal and Jaques Samuel Pianos Prize, and later completed a master’s at the University of Connecticut. He toured with the Backman Trio, whose CD was recommended in Gramophone.
Marcus is a regular accompanist at London conservatoires and the Tunbridge Wells International Music Competition, where he won the accompanist prize. He is Head of Keyboard at Tonbridge School and also teaches at Highgate School.

description:
Join Sarah Raven and Adam Nicolson for a rare evening together, sharing the inside story of two remarkable gardens – Sissinghurst Castle and Perch Hill – and the family, ideas and history that connect them.
Adam grew up at Sissinghurst with his grandparents, Vita Sackville-West and Harold Nicolson. Vita was a celebrated writer and the creative force behind one of England’s most influential gardens; Harold an MP and writer who gave the garden its enduring structure.
Adam and Sarah returned to Sissinghurst in 2004 with their young family, while just a few miles away Sarah continued to create the world-famous garden at Perch Hill.
Together, Sarah and Adam will explore these two very different places: Sissinghurst, steeped in memory and nostalgia, and Perch Hill, colourful, experimental and always looking forward.
Through their personal stories, you’ll discover how each garden has evolved, the people and ideas that have shaped them, and what gardens can give us in return.

description:
Join us at The Amelia for our monthly learning sessions open to home educated children across the borough.
Our learning sessions are linked to The Amelia’s collections, are based on enquiry-led learning and are rooted in the National Curriculum. Sessions provide unique opportunities for object-handling and inspiring activities to guide children and their families as they explore our galleries.
Duration: Standard sessions last 60 mins
We aim to provide a fully inclusive service for all our young visitors. Please let us know if there are any SPLD/ or accessibility needs we should be aware of so that we can help support all participants to engage with the session.
Please note, children must be accompanied by their parent/carers and remain their responsibility at all times.
Monthly themes:
8 September – Archaeology Adventure
Join us for a special exhibition-linked session. The group will start with an introduction to archaeology in the Learning Room, with the chance to explore artefacts and objects hands-on. The session will conclude in Archaeology Adventure, our current temporary exhibition.
13 October – The Story of the Wells – Local History
In this session, the group will discover how and why our town came into existence. Using artefacts to piece together its story from forest, to popular health resort, to holiday destination for a princess, the group will also find out why children from the East End of London would spend their summer holidays here 100 years ago!
10 November – Dinosaurs and Fossils
In this session, the group are cast as palaeontologists and explore clues about what the world was like millions of years ago. They have the chance to handle a range of fossils from The Amelia’s Collection to investigate how they were made and what they tell us about the past.
8 December – Generations of Joy
This session will take place off-site and provide an enriching opportunity for inter-generational engagement, with children and care-home residents taking part in Christmas-themed activities together.

title: Take a Closer Look: Howard Hodgkin
description:
Join a Curator from The Amelia for a short guided tour of the current temporary exhibition Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden. Whether you already know the works of Howard Hodgkin, or are curious to learn more, join us to take a closer look.
About the exhibition:
This autumn, The Amelia Scott presents Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden, a critically acclaimed exhibition bringing together more than 30 prints spanning five decades of the artist’s career, from 1966 to 2016.
Originally developed by Pitzhanger Manor & Gallery, this landmark exhibition showcases the work of Howard Hodgkin, whose vivid use of colour, expressive brushwork and deeply personal approach to abstraction made him one of Britain’s most distinctive post-war artists.
Featuring bold, gestural compositions that explore memory, emotion and place, the exhibition immerses visitors in Hodgkin’s unique visual world. The selected prints reveal the important role printmaking played throughout his practice and demonstrate his extraordinary ability to transform fleeting experiences into powerful images.

description:
Get into the festive spirit with this joyful Christmas knitting workshop, where you’ll design and make a selection of handmade decorations for your tree.

About your facilitator – Monica Russel.
Monica is a knitwear designer and teacher who loves working and designing with colours and being creative with her designs. She has run her business The Knitknacks for 14 years during which she has developed a reputation for her Fair Isle patterns and her ability to teach knitting to beginners and advanced learners who wish to expand their skills.

title: Home Education at The Amelia - Primary
description:
Join us at The Amelia for our monthly learning sessions open to home educated children across the borough.
Our learning sessions are linked to The Amelia’s collections, are based on enquiry-led learning and are rooted in the National Curriculum. Sessions provide unique opportunities for object-handling and inspiring activities to guide children and their families as they explore our galleries.
Duration: Standard sessions last 60 mins
We aim to provide a fully inclusive service for all our young visitors. Please let us know if there are any SPLD/ or accessibility needs we should be aware of so that we can help support all participants to engage with the session.
Please note, children must be accompanied by their parent/carers and remain their responsibility at all times.
Monthly themes:
8 September – Archaeology Adventure
Join us for a special exhibition-linked session. The group will start with an introduction to archaeology in the Learning Room, with the chance to explore artefacts and objects hands-on. The session will conclude in Archaeology Adventure, our current temporary exhibition.
13 October – The Story of the Wells – Local History
In this session, the group will discover how and why our town came into existence. Using artefacts to piece together its story from forest, to popular health resort, to holiday destination for a princess, the group will also find out why children from the East End of London would spend their summer holidays here 100 years ago!
10 November – Dinosaurs and Fossils
In this session, the group are cast as palaeontologists and explore clues about what the world was like millions of years ago. They have the chance to handle a range of fossils from The Amelia’s Collection to investigate how they were made and what they tell us about the past.
8 December – Generations of Joy
This session will take place off-site and provide an enriching opportunity for inter-generational engagement, with children and care-home residents taking part in Christmas-themed activities together.
Sessions beyond December will be available to book later in the year.

title: Take a Closer Look: Howard Hodgkin
description:
Join a Curator from The Amelia for a short guided tour of the current temporary exhibition Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden. Whether you already know the works of Howard Hodgkin, or are curious to learn more, join us to take a closer look.
About the exhibition:
This autumn, The Amelia Scott presents Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden, a critically acclaimed exhibition bringing together more than 30 prints spanning five decades of the artist’s career, from 1966 to 2016.
Originally developed by Pitzhanger Manor & Gallery, this landmark exhibition showcases the work of Howard Hodgkin, whose vivid use of colour, expressive brushwork and deeply personal approach to abstraction made him one of Britain’s most distinctive post-war artists.
Featuring bold, gestural compositions that explore memory, emotion and place, the exhibition immerses visitors in Hodgkin’s unique visual world. The selected prints reveal the important role printmaking played throughout his practice and demonstrate his extraordinary ability to transform fleeting experiences into powerful images.

title: Take a Closer Look: Howard Hodgkin
description:
Join a Curator from The Amelia for a short guided tour of the current temporary exhibition Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden. Whether you already know the works of Howard Hodgkin, or are curious to learn more, join us to take a closer look.
About the exhibition:
This autumn, The Amelia Scott presents Howard Hodgkin: In a Public Garden, a critically acclaimed exhibition bringing together more than 30 prints spanning five decades of the artist’s career, from 1966 to 2016.
Originally developed by Pitzhanger Manor & Gallery, this landmark exhibition showcases the work of Howard Hodgkin, whose vivid use of colour, expressive brushwork and deeply personal approach to abstraction made him one of Britain’s most distinctive post-war artists.
Featuring bold, gestural compositions that explore memory, emotion and place, the exhibition immerses visitors in Hodgkin’s unique visual world. The selected prints reveal the important role printmaking played throughout his practice and demonstrate his extraordinary ability to transform fleeting experiences into powerful images.

title: Sensing Culture: Group for blind & partially sighted adults
description:
Blind and partially sighted adults are invited to explore The Amelia’s collections through touch, sound and imagination.

Sessions take place monthly, on the last Friday of each month, from 10:30am to 12:30pm, in the Artist Residency Studio at The Amelia Scott.

• Object Handling: Explore authentic museum objects through guided touch with support from our trained staff.
• Tactile Tours: Take part in sensory-led journeys through our galleries and private tours of temporary exhibitions.
• Creative Making: Try out different materials and create your own artwork inspired by the collection.
No previous art experience needed.

description:
Your Place to Be is a monthly group for those who are caring for someone. 
If you are supporting someone with mental health difficulties, physical care needs, Alzheimer’s, dementia, or a neurodiverse child, it is important to take care of yourself.

title: Home Education at The Amelia - Primary
description:
Join us at The Amelia for our monthly learning sessions open to home educated children across the borough.
Our learning sessions are linked to The Amelia’s collections, are based on enquiry-led learning and are rooted in the National Curriculum. Sessions provide unique opportunities for object-handling and inspiring activities to guide children and their families as they explore our galleries.
Duration: Standard sessions last 60 mins
We aim to provide a fully inclusive service for all our young visitors. Please let us know if there are any SPLD/ or accessibility needs we should be aware of so that we can help support all participants to engage with the session.
Please note, children must be accompanied by their parent/carers and remain their responsibility at all times.
Monthly themes:
8 September – Archaeology Adventure
Join us for a special exhibition-linked session. The group will start with an introduction to archaeology in the Learning Room, with the chance to explore artefacts and objects hands-on. The session will conclude in Archaeology Adventure, our current temporary exhibition.
13 October – The Story of the Wells – Local History
In this session, the group will discover how and why our town came into existence. Using artefacts to piece together its story from forest, to popular health resort, to holiday destination for a princess, the group will also find out why children from the East End of London would spend their summer holidays here 100 years ago!
10 November – Dinosaurs and Fossils
In this session, the group are cast as palaeontologists and explore clues about what the world was like millions of years ago. They have the chance to handle a range of fossils from The Amelia’s Collection to investigate how they were made and what they tell us about the past.
8 December – Generations of Joy
This session will take place off-site and provide an enriching opportunity for inter-generational engagement, with children and care-home residents taking part in Christmas-themed activities together.

Contact us to find out more before booking

These sessions will take place in the Children’s library (under the beautiful night sky) on Tuesdays at 10:00 and 11:00, and Thursdays at 10:00.
No need to book, just drop in!
